hook: A 1900 house identified as a historic resource, with $620,000 of permitted work between 2019 and 2021.

permits.description: garage expansion and foundation replacement; living space added at basement
revised den access to rear patio; new rear yard landscaping
interior remodel of two baths, half bath relocated at main level, new sliding doors at den
kitchen, powder room and pantry remodel with new electrical
roof replaced with roof deck serving a second-floor bedroom; windows and doors replaced at area of work
bathroom remodel with new plumbing and electrical
rotted wall removed and replaced; footing and stair rail raised
cap footings and provide two additional shear walls

historical_record.description: Offered new with 742 and 744 at $5,250 — reception hall, parlors, dining room, kitchen, four bedrooms and a finished basement, with sanitary plumbing and steam heating throughout; lots 25 × 125 feet. Agents Tobin & McNally.
Advertised for sale as a standing residence.

unknowns.year_built_conflict: The assessor gives 1900, but the house was advertised for sale in March 1895 and offered as new in September 1895.

historic_survey.note: Put forward as a potential San Francisco Landmark for its association with the builder Charles Hinkel (1847-1908) and his sons, all prolific home builders in Eureka Valley and San Francisco, and as a distinctive example of Queen Anne architecture. The statement dates the house to 1892 where it lists Hinkel's work and says he moved to it in 1891 where it recommends the landmarking; it gives his death as 1908 in one place and as some time between 1900 and 1910 in another. The statement is reconnaissance-level and says inclusion in it is not a judgement on a building's worthiness for preservation.
